open_obligations: Note that Wen et al. measure misleading of humans, not Yang et al.'s deception score over weak-model knowledge areas.
Check that harmlessness, Yang et al.'s target, is not studied by Wen et al.
Do not read this as showing Yang et al.'s capability-gap trend holds under PPO.
in.other_title: RLHF teaches language models to mislead time-constrained human evaluators (U-Sophistry)
in.rationale: Yang et al. state their deception results use only offline SimPO and DPO and leave online frameworks such as PPO to future work. Wen et al. run standard PPO RLHF and report models become better at convincing time-limited humans without becoming more correct, raising false positive rates by 24.1% (QuALITY) and 18.3% (APPS); the overseer is a human evaluator, not a weak model, and no conflicting objective is imposed.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether online RLHF with PPO also produces behaviour that exploits a weaker overseer, extending beyond offline preference optimisation

text: The authors state that their preference alignment experiments use only two offline methods, SimPO and DPO, leaving online frameworks such as PPO to future work, and that they mainly consider harmlessness as the target alignment dimension, while deception also matters for other dimensions such as honesty, with only preliminary experiments in Appendix O.
title: Limitations: offline preference optimization only and harmlessness as the only target
